blocks: "X rather than Y" / "X instead of Y" when Y is only there as a foil for X
Don't frame a claim as a binary correction of something the reader never asserted. The common shapes are:
Both make the reader hold a discarded foil to receive one fact. State Y (or X) in the positive and stop.
Avoid: "It's not a config bug — it's a race in the watcher."
Prefer: "There's a race in the watcher."
Avoid: "Use a soft link rather than copying the file."
Prefer: "Use a soft link." (Add "copying would drift" only if that foil passes the negation test above.)
Ordinary comparison stays allowed when both sides are live options the reader is choosing between, and the contrast itself is the point.
Don't add a "won't do" section to a plan unless My/AI/Rule/Prune useless commandments still leaves something that qualifies under the test above. Default to describing only what will happen.

When something is worth keeping past this session — a preference of mine, a project fact, how I want a piece of work done — write it into the git repository or knowledge garden the work is in, as a tracked file any tool can open. In this graph, a standing instruction for agents goes under My/AI/Rule, which agents read at load; a preference of mine goes under My/Pref.

I move between coding agents all day, and each one keeps its notes where only it looks. Claude/Code saves to ~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/ and reads ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md. Codex reads ~/.codex/AGENTS.md. CursorAI has its own project rules. A note left in any of those is invisible to the next agent I open, and it sits outside the repository the work lives in.
Leave your harness's own memory system alone until I authorize the memory going there.
